subject: gr-qc
authors: J. M. Isidro, B. Koch, A. Rincon
abstract: Based on Landauer's principle, we provide a geometrical definition for the entropy of a given static, spherically symmetric spacetime. Considering a congruence of geodesics across a surface, one defines the entropy of a congruence as the surface integral of the entropy of the constituent geodesics. Under certain mild assumptions, we establish a second law for the entropy function thus defined (Landauer entropy), and relate it to Bekenstein-Hawking entropy.
title_relatable: Can erasing information explain why black holes have entropy?
hook: Landauer's principle — erasing a bit generates heat — may give spacetime geometry its own entropy law.
summary: By treating bundles of geodesics as information carriers and invoking Landauer's principle (erasing information produces entropy), the authors assign an entropy to any static, spherically symmetric spacetime via a surface integral. They show this 'Landauer entropy' obeys a second law and connects to the familiar Bekenstein-Hawking black hole entropy. If the link holds, it grounds the thermodynamics of spacetime in the same information-theoretic reasoning behind ordinary computing.
